definitions.gloss: physical stance of readiness; defensive posture
definitions.explanation: A body posture taken in preparation for a physical confrontation, attack, or sudden movement. Used in martial arts and sports.

definitions.gloss: mental readiness; bracing oneself; being on guard
definitions.explanation: A figurative stance of psychological preparedness or wariness, as when anticipating difficulty, criticism, or an uncomfortable situation.

examples.japanese: {相手|あいて}の{攻撃|こうげき}に{備|そな}えて{身構|みがま}えた。
examples.english: He braced himself for the opponent's attack.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}の{揺|ゆ}れを{感|かん}じて、とっさに{身構|みがま}えた。
examples.english: Feeling the earthquake tremor, I instinctively braced myself.

examples.japanese: そんなに{身構|みがま}えなくてもいいよ。
examples.english: You don't need to be so on guard.

examples.japanese: {面接|めんせつ}と{聞|き}いて{身構|みがま}えてしまう。
examples.english: I tense up when I hear the word 'interview.'

examples.japanese: {初対面|しょたいめん}の{人|ひと}には、つい{身構|みがま}えてしまうことがある。
examples.english: I sometimes find myself being guarded around people I meet for the first time.

notes:
Noun form of the verb {身構|みがま}える (to take a stance; to brace oneself). From {身|み} (body/self) + {構|かま}える (to set up; to assume a position). The noun form refers to both the physical posture and the psychological state of readiness.

The verb form {身構|みがま}える is more common in everyday use. The noun {身構|みがま}え appears in descriptions of stances and attitudes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {身構|みがま}えを{取|と}る: to assume a ready stance
- {身構|みがま}えを{解|と}く: to relax one's guard
- つい{身構|みがま}えてしまう: to involuntarily tense up

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {構|かま}え: stance; posture — more general, used in martial arts for any fighting stance
- {警戒|けいかい}: vigilance; caution — focuses on being watchful against danger
- {緊張|きんちょう}: tension; nervousness — describes the internal feeling rather than the outward readiness
